note: Advisories that check-npm-audit.mjs must not fail on. Only add an entry when NO published version resolves the advisory — if a newer pin fixes it, raise the pin in TemplateVersions.kt instead. Entries are keyed by GHSA id, never by package name, so a future unrelated vulnerability in the same package still fails the gate. Every entry needs a reason, a url, a reviewed date, and an expires date; expiry is reported as a warning, not a failure.

allow.reason: No fixed version exists upstream. The advisory covers image-size <=2.0.2, and 2.0.2 is the latest published release, so there is nothing to bump to. It reaches the templates through react-native -> metro -> image-size ^1.0.2, and metro still declares that same range in 0.87.0. npm suggests react-native@0.72.17, which is a large downgrade from the 0.85.x line the templates target and does not resolve the advisory anyway. Impact is a denial of service in an image parser used by the React Native bundler at build time.

Same package, same dependency path, and the same lack of any fixed release as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr — this advisory covers the JXL and HEIF parsers rather than ICNS. Remove both entries together once metro depends on an image-size release outside the vulnerable range.
